origin: Devised by Ben Shneiderman in the early 1990s to see which folders took up space on a hard disk. It means laying out a tree structure like a map.
whenToUse: Many items make up a whole, such as storage or a budget.
You show which items take up most of it.
There are more than five items, too many for a pie chart.
whenNotToUse: Similar sizes must be compared precisely (use a bar chart).
Change over time (use an area chart).
There are only two or three items (use a pie chart).

alternatives.name: Pie Chart
alternatives.reason: There are only a few items.

accessibility: Items are told apart by the names and values in the cells, not color.
Small cells read their name and share when pointed at.
The table view lists every item and share.
